title: Chroma MCP Server
summary: Create Chroma collections and add, query and inspect embeddings from your coding agent with the chroma-mcp server, run through uvx.
description: Chroma's MCP server turns the agent into a client of a Chroma database. It can create and modify collections, add documents with metadata, run semantic queries, fetch by id or filter, and delete what you no longer need.

You choose where the data lives with a client type: ephemeral keeps everything in memory, persistent writes to a folder you name, and http or cloud connect to a running Chroma. The server starts with uvx, so uv must be installed. The default embedding function needs no key.
useWhen: Try a retrieval idea on a handful of documents in memory
Keep a persistent local collection of notes and search it
Inspect what a collection holds before debugging a RAG pipeline
Compare how two embedding settings rank the same query

mcp.name: chroma

env.name: CHROMA_DATA_DIR
env.description: Folder for data when the client type is persistent

access: Reads and queries collections in the Chroma instance you choose
Can create, change and delete collections and documents

example.prompt: Create a collection named meeting-notes, add these three paragraphs, then query it for 'budget concerns'.
example.result: Collection meeting-notes created with 3 documents. Best match: paragraph 2, about the Q3 budget overrun, distance 0.31.

faq.question: Where is my data kept?
faq.answer: It depends on the client type. Ephemeral is lost when the server stops; persistent uses CHROMA_DATA_DIR.

faq.question: Can I keep API keys out of the config?
faq.answer: Yes. The README supports a dotenv file through --dotenv-path, and cloud settings also come from CHROMA_ environment variables.

faq.question: Does it have a read-only mode?
faq.answer: Not documented. Delete tools are included, so use a persistent folder you can restore, or ask the agent to confirm before deletions.

access: Reads collections from the configured Chroma
Can modify and delete collections and documents
